R9322.summary: f. 121: Hieronymus Łaski to a Bavarian duke, Buda 24 Nov 1529: the Sultan, forced home by plague in his army, left King John the kingdom of Hungary without tribute, with fifty guns and powder, and will return next summer against Ferdinand's lands unless there is a concord. f. 122: King John of Hungary to Duke Ludwig of Bavaria, sending Lazarus the Jew as envoy.
R9322.en:
It cannot be said, most illustrious prince and my most respected lord, how welcome to [D] were the counsels of Your
Most Illustrious Lordship, for which [F] gives Your Most Illustrious Lordship great thanks; and in all things His
Majesty has followed the counsels of Your Lordship, for His Majesty has written to Duke [?Frederick], captain of the
Roman Empire, [?all] that Your Lordship [?advised]. And let Your Most Illustrious Lordship know tha[t] [F] is inclined
and ready for all things whatsoever [?may] regard the [h]onour, dignity and advantage of Your Lordship, and counts you
among his first and dearest friends.

This is the news:

R9417.summary: Łaski to the dukes' secretary Waisenfelder, Kraków 16 June [1530]: concord best made through the imperial princes; Nicolaus Minkuics sent to the King of France and to meet the dukes' envoys at Coburg on 4 July (the roads were beset); the Sultan, persuaded to a year's truce, will receive whom King John names and will come next summer by land and sea unless there is concord; the King of Poland's daughter: the match starts coldly while someone presses through Sigismund Herberstein for Frederick the Count Palatine; the dukes should send to Charles V to hold back his brother from attacking King John. Signed 'Lask', in his own hand.

R9323.summary: Latin note from Łaski's circle to the Bavarian secretary: [FLW] loves the Duke of Bavaria; Łaski wants concord between King John and Ferdinand, for without it Bohemia will perish and the Turks will consume it and Austria; the other princes' lands have nothing to fear by his pact with the Turk unless the Imperial estates aid Ferdinand against [FLW]; the Turks are not to be despised; he would have sent horses to the Sultan; commends himself to the dukes.
R9323.en: Dearest Lord Secretary, know that [FLW] loves the Duke of Bavaria most sincerely and is willing to do everything for them; but I greatly desire concord between [King John] and [Ferdinand], for it is certain that if there is no concord Bohemia will perish, which the Turks will consume as they will Austria. The lands of the other princes, however, [?fear] nothing, because I have made such a pact with the Turk, unless perhaps the estates of the Empire alone want the Turk's hostility by giving aid to Ferdinand against [FLW]. So let your princes and the whole Empire take care not to stir up the Turks against themselves; nor are the Turks [?to be despised], for few know their power and their cunning. I would most gladly have sent horses to the Turkish prince, [?common] to us, but [...] would not take them. May your lordship commend me to his princes, for I am assuredly their servant.

R9403.summary: Łaski to a councillor of the Bavarian dukes, 17 Sept 1531: the Sultan told Ferdinand's envoys there would be no peace or truce unless Hungary is given up to King John, and is preparing ships, guns and grain on the Danube; Łaski will ride to the Speyer diet and asks the dukes to stop any decision against the king; the royal marriage will be settled with the King of Poland.
R9403.en:
Noble and excellent lord, dearest friend, greeting and my commendation. On the fifteenth of this month Ruffus brought
me his letters; how welcome they were first to [DAG = King John], and then therefore all that they contained in his
letters was understood, and abundantly. Whereas Your Lordship promises me the favour of your princes and declares the
goodwill of Their Most Illustrious Lordships towards me, it cheers and gladdens me with great joy, as one who from my
earliest age has always wished and sought nothing more than to win for myself the grace and favour of princes and
great men; and that very thing I shall do with all zeal, now and always hereafter, and I shall serve the most
illustrious princes of Your Lordship with my person and all my means.

system: Łaski's graphic cipher (System B of the volume): one sign per letter (21 letter signs, W serving c and t), a few word signs (DAG = King John, BIGX = Ferdinand, FLW probably King John's title), no word division marks beyond spaces. In R9403 (1531) the signs…
